entries.0c9b4126a2190e2b: This is the core business of the company group, manufacturing and selling sporting goods for badminton, tennis, golf and other sports.
entries.0ed0fd5ee7c601bd: A manufacturer that, centered on badminton, makes sporting goods such as rackets and shuttlecocks and sells them in Japan and overseas.
entries.14391da6ff826866: This segment is handled by local subsidiaries in Asia. The securities report explains that sales are handled by local subsidiaries in Taiwan and China, and manufacturing by local subsidiaries in Taiwan, India and Thailand. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥85,562 million (up 25.8% year on year), and operating profit was ¥11,864 million (up 22.2% year on year). This is the segment with the largest revenue from external customers among the 5 reportable segments. According to the notes, China accounts for ¥77,756 million of this. The securities report explains that at the Chinese sales subsidiary, badminton equipment, other equipment such as wear and bags, and tennis equipment also grew, centered on badminton equipment.
entries.261bc11c03a5cf20: This segment is handled by local subsidiaries in Asia.
entries.6378bdff375ee083: This is the core business of the company group, manufacturing and selling sporting goods for badminton, tennis, golf and other sports. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥163,091 million, accounting for most of consolidated revenue of ¥163,643 million. Revenue by product category was: badminton equipment ¥101,707 million, tennis equipment ¥21,983 million, golf equipment ¥1,460 million, and other equipment, including wear and bags, ¥37,939 million. Manufacturing is carried out at domestic manufacturing sites and also at local subsidiaries in Asia (Taiwan, India and Thailand). Sales are handled by the company in Japan and, overseas, by local subsidiaries and leading distributors in each country. The securities report discloses this business divided into 4 reportable segments by region (Japan, Asia, North America and Europe), based on the sales structure.
entries.707d325d332de01a: This segment is handled by local subsidiaries in Europe (the United Kingdom and Germany), and the consolidated subsidiaries are YONEX U.K. LIMITED and YONEX GmbH. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥6,077 million (up 13.4% year on year), and operating profit was ¥506 million (up 6.2% year on year). The securities report explains that badminton equipment grew due to heightened interest in the sport from the hosting of international tournaments, among other factors, and tennis rackets grew due to improved brand recognition from the performance of sponsored players.
entries.76bfc2981ba0944e: This is its starting point as a listed company.
entries.a01c417720ffc7c0: A category handled by the local subsidiaries in North America (the United States and Canada); the consolidated subsidiary listed is YONEX CORPORATION of the United States.
entries.a72660cbea22f651: This segment is where the company (the filing company) handles domestic sales and exports and intermediary trade to overseas distributors. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥64,092 million (up 10.5% year on year), and operating profit was ¥3,962 million (up 7.3% year on year). The securities report explains that in Japan, badminton rackets and strings and tennis rackets and shoes, among others, grew; for overseas distributors, badminton equipment remained firm, centered on Asia, and sales also grew in Europe. Because this segment is divided based on the sales structure, its amount differs from Japan revenue of ¥41,874 million under “Information by Region,” which is divided by customer location.

entries.bbd56525b0af9345: This business operates golf courses, golf driving ranges and tennis clubs, and is conducted solely by the company in Japan. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥552 million (down 0.8% year on year), and operating loss was ¥22 million (operating profit of ¥16 million in the prior year). The securities report explains that at the core Yonex Country Club, although affected by intense summer heat and winter snow, the number of visitors increased and revenue rose slightly, while at other facilities revenue fell due to operating restrictions and other effects of poor weather. The loss is stated to be due to increased facility repair costs and other factors.
entries.c624401c73d27589: This business operates golf courses, golf driving ranges and tennis clubs, and is conducted solely by the company in Japan.
entries.d2090b777e1e4050: This segment is where the company (the filing company) handles domestic sales and exports and intermediary trade to overseas distributors.
entries.f425b57305c8b64d: This category is handled by local subsidiaries in North America (the United States and Canada), and the consolidated subsidiary listed is YONEX CORPORATION of the United States. Net sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥7,358 million (up 15.8% from the previous year), and operating profit was ¥256 million (down 54.2% from the previous year). The securities report explains that revenue increased as badminton products and other products such as tennis rackets and apparel grew, while profit decreased because selling, general and administrative expenses rose, owing to personnel costs and advertising expenses as well as the cost of efforts to strengthen direct contact with consumers through EC sites and pop-up stores.
